title: Explicit dihedral relation ideal is never produced (reduction to algorithm only)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: The problem asks to *determine explicitly* and *give generators of* the relation ideal $I$ for **every** stratum. For the dihedral (and non-cyclic) case the solution's actual output is only "$I=\ker\Phi$, computed mechanically by the elimination Algorithm 1" (Thm 3.3(e), §6, Prop 5.x, Cor 7.x). That is a *computability/termination* statement, not an explicit generating set. No closed-form generators, and no explicit proven-correct generating family, are given for the dihedral case beyond the $g=2$ example. The solution itself concedes this in 'Scope and honesty'. Whether a terminating (worst-case doubly-exponential) Gröbner computation constitutes 'explicit determination' is the crux; under the benchmark standard it does not. This is the central gap.
